The man and the woman are living in the garden, with only one command to keep. Now a new character arrives: the serpent, described as more crafty than any other creature God has made. The consequences are spoken over the serpent, the woman and the man in turn, and they touch everything: work, childbirth, relationships, and death itself. Yet within the judgement on the serpent is a hint of hope that later readers would treasure, a promise that the woman's offspring will one day crush its head.
